title: Improved Visualization and Quantitative Analysis of Drug Effects Using Micropatterned Cells
protocol: Place 2 CYTOOchips in 2 independent wells of a 6 well plate.
Ensure that you read "CYTOO" in the lower right corner of the CYTOOchip.
Collect HeLa cells (~80% confluent) by trypsinization.
Check under a microscope that cells are properly dispersed by the trypsin treatment.
Centrifuge collected cells at 300g for 4 min.
Gently resuspend the cell pellet after centrifugation.
Count cells and dilute to a concentration of 15,000 cells/mL in completed DMEM/F12 culture media.
Dispense 4 mL (60,000 cells) into each well containing a CYTOOchip.
Let the cells sediment for 10 min under the hood.
Move the plate with cells to the cell incubator after 10 min.
Check regularly under the microscope as soon as cells have attached.
Change the cell medium and gently flush the coverslip surface by aspirating from the side of the well when cells attach.
Never let the chip dry out during the procedure.
Add 4 mL PBS and aspirate again first starting at the center of the chip then moving to the side of the well.
Aspirate off the PBS without exposing the chip to air.
Repeat washing with PBS 3-4 times.
Check under the microscope for floating cells.
If many floating cells remain, repeat the washing procedure.
If few cells are observed, aspirate part of the PBS and replace it with 2 mL fresh medium.
Aspirate and add 4 mL of fresh medium twice.
Place the plate in a tissue culture incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2 for a minimum of three hours to allow cells to achieve full spreading.
Dissolve blebbistatin in 100% DMSO to obtain a stock solution of 17 mM.
Dilute the stock solution further to 5 mM with 100% DMSO.
Make a final dilution in culture medium to obtain a final concentration of 5 μM blebbistatin in 0.1% DMSO.
Prepare 4 mL of medium containing 0.1% DMSO only for control conditions.
Aspirate the media on cells and replace it with 4 mL medium prepared for treated and control conditions.
Incubate cells for 1 hour at 37°C.
Prepare cytoskeleton buffer (CB) as per the reagent section instructions.
Add 1 g of sucrose to 2 mL of CB to make 1xCB-sucrose.
Include sucrose in the 1xCB-sucrose to preserve internal cell structures.
Add 1 mL of 1xCB-sucrose to 4 mL of warm PFA 5% solution to prepare 4% PFA-CB-sucrose.
Incubate CYTOOchip in a well containing 2 mL of 4% PFA-CB-sucrose solution for 10 min at room temperature (RT).
Remove PFA-CB-sucrose and wash once with PBS.
Wash the CYTOOchip again with 2 mL of 100 mM NH4Cl for 10 min to quench residual PFA crosslinking activity.
Store PFA fixed slides in PBS at 4°C before staining for fluorescent imaging if needed.
Remove NH4Cl and add 2 mL/well of 0.1% Triton X-100-CB solution for permeabilization of cell membrane for 3 min at RT.
Wash the CYTOOchip twice with 2 mL PBS to remove detergent.
Stain actin filaments with fluorescent-phalloidin which binds specifically to native actin.
Add 2 mL of FITC-conjugated phalloidin diluted 1:2000 in PBS with 1.5% BSA.
Incubate for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash once with 2 mL PBS.
Add 2 mL of Hoechst (1 μg/mL in PBS).
Incubate for 3 minutes at room temperature.
Wash twice with 2 mL PBS.
Mount CYTOOchip onto a standard microscope slide using 25-30 μL of Mowiol or another mounting solution.
Select 20x magnification.
Open Multidimensional Acquisition and set up the experiment parameters: Number of wavelengths to 3, Wavelength types to DAPI, FITC, Cy3.
Set exposure time for each wavelength.
Perform autofocus on each wavelength.
Select where to save data.
Select Cy3 wavelength and position the camera so that 12 micropatterns are visualized and centered in the camera field (4 columns and 3 rows of patterns).
Create a journal running MultiDimensional Acquisition.
Open Scan stage function from Devices/Stage/Scan Stage menu.
Enter 6 columns and 4 rows with -400 μm X step size and 300 μm Y step size to acquire 24 images each containing 12 micropatterns at 20x magnification.
In Set Journal to Execute, upload the journal MDA.JNL.
Press Scan to start the automated acquisition of the whole block in the three wavelengths.
Create image stacks for all three channels centered on micropatterns.
Use micropatterns to avoid cell clustering and clumping.
Define regions centered on the micropatterns using fluorescently labeled images.
Transpose defined regions onto images acquired in other channels.
Crop corresponding images from each channel.
Assemble cropped images into stacks for each wavelength.
Create an RGB-stack by merging the three channels.
Apply a single cell selection filter to detect the number of nuclei per image.
Eliminate stacks containing more than one nucleus or no nuclei.
Eliminate non-normalized cells using a cell area cut-off filter.
Remove dividing cells by applying a FITC channel actin filter.
Calculate cell area and remove cells below a certain size cutoff.
Determine the cell envelope area based on the micropattern size.
Align cell images using the MultiStackReg ImageJ plugin.
Generate aligned stacks of individual images for further analysis.
Build a Reference Cell from the aligned image stacks.
Growing cells on micropatterns ensures all cells have similar shapes.
Construct the Reference Cell in ImageJ by making a projection of filtered and aligned images from a stack using median projection method.
Apply LUT (Look Up Tables) converting monocolor image into a color-coded frequency map for examination.
Measure changes in curvature of actin stress fibers.
Stain for intensity measurement of actin stress fibers.
Measure length or thickness of actin stress fibers.
Assess morphometric features of actin filaments or cell shape.
Count the number of collapsed cells using ImageJ macro Hypotenuse.
Define a theoretical hypotenuse of the cell triangle shape from thresholded images.
Threshold actin-stained images to approximate actual cell shape.
Measure the area between theoretical hypotenuse and actual concave cell membrane.
